data.narrative:
Westmag is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector peer set of 8 private companies and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), including named peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable and provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($11M) as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier to reflect progression toward Series A, this approach implies a valuation of $28M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient data density—while 8 companies operate in Robotics & Manufacturing, only one occupies Westmag's narrow peer tier (same stage, similar valuation band), falling short of the three-datapoint minimum needed for robust cross-sectional analysis.

The triangulated valuation range is $23M (low), $28M (median), and $32M (high). The median estimate of $28M rests on a single methodological pillar, creating material uncertainty. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for this sector's fundraising cadence, the degree to which named peers provide valid comparables given heterogeneity in robotics subsectors, and the limited public market evidence (one public comp) for validation. Investors should treat this range as indicative pending broader peer data or revenue/traction metrics.
